- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; lag correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of lag.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.5–0.8), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
- When sentiment is uniformly low (≤0.2) for 5+ days, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for suppressed demand or policy effects.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model is consistently 5–8% above true outcome, apply a 1–2% downward bias correction unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
